name: Suruí
sweep_summary: The single sweep item (Massini-Cagliari 1995, Glottolog 633904) is a Glottolog machine mis-assignment ('computerized assignment from "percurso"') about the history of Portuguese stress — irrelevant to Suruí. The real yield of the sweep is that the previously 'SOURCE-NAMED-UNREACHABLE' van der Meer 1982 Unicamp thesis (Fonologia da língua Suruí) and the previously 'NOT LOCATED' Guerra 2004 ULB thesis are both fully scanned in the Museu do Índio's DocReader library (app.docvirt.com/mi_bibliografico, folders 8954 and 8677); all 75 + 105 page images were fetched sources, scanned (por/eng), assembled into PDFs and with. Van der Meer 1982 pp. 24-30 gives the first-hand stress statement: Suruí is tonal (2 tones) and word stress is free/lexical, normally on a high-tone syllable but not predictable from tone, with the one condition that a stressed final low-tone syllable must be heavy (long or closed); three stress degrees, enclitic-triggered shift to the verb's final syllable, and phrasal rhythmic alternation. Guerra 2004 (tone only) and Surui 2020 (no phonology; cites van der Meer for tone and accent) are silent on stress; Yvinec & Suruí 2017 (LangSci, open) only documents the acute = high-tone orthography. Bontkes 1978 dictionary and Bontkes & Bontkes 1978 phonemic analysis remain unread (SIL archive Cloudflare-blocked; Museu do Índio holds only the dictionary's title card), low priority. Language is not in the catalog; van der Meer 1982 p. 28 is the recommended deciding source if it is added.

new_statements.quote: a) Quanto à posição da sílaba acentuada na palavra, esta parece ser livre, com talvez uma única condição para acentuação nas sílabas finais de tom baixo na presença de outras (não proclíticas) de tom alto. Estas parecem só poder ser acentuadas se forem sílabas fortes, isto é, se forem longas ou fechadas. Se o acento provier dos deslocamentos acima citados, que descreveremos mais a fundo logo abaixo, esta condição não é necessária.
new_statements.translation: a) As to the position of the stressed syllable in the word, it appears to be free, with perhaps a single condition on the stressing of final low-tone syllables in the presence of other (non-proclitic) high-tone syllables: these seem to be stressable only if they are strong syllables, i.e. long or closed. If the stress comes from the shifts mentioned above, which we describe in more depth below, this condition is not necessary.
new_statements.citation: van der Meer, Tine H. (1982). Fonologia da língua Suruí. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Estadual de Campinas, 75 pp.
new_statements.locator: Ch. III-B 'Tom e acentuação', '2) Acento', §a), p. 28 (position of stress); framing statement p. 26
new_statements.reading: Suruí (Paiter) is a two-tone language in which word stress is a separate, lexically FREE (unpredictable) property: it usually coincides with a high-tone syllable but cannot be predicted from tone (p. 26: 'não haver como predizer onde cairá o acento'); the only restriction is a weight condition on stressed final low-tone syllables (must be long or closed). Stress has three degrees, shifts to the verb's final syllable before enclitics, and undergoes rhythmic alternation within genitive/verbal phrases (pp. 27-30). The p. 28 word list shows initial, penultimate and final stress on otherwise comparable words. For a catalog coding this is 'lexical/free stress (tone-correlated), with a weight condition on final syllables' — not a fixed-position system. Verified against the page image; scanned text also saved.

sources.quote: p. 28: "a) Quanto à posição da sílaba acentuada na palavra, esta parece ser livre, com talvez uma única condição para acentuação nas sílabas finais de tom baixo na presença de outras (não proclíticas) de tom alto. Estas parecem só poder ser acentuadas se forem sílabas fortes, isto é, se forem longas ou fechadas. Se o acento provier dos deslocamentos acima citados, que descreveremos mais a fundo logo abaixo, esta condição não é necessária." — p. 26: "Embora, a nível de palavra, o acento normalmente coincida com sílaba de tom alto, a acentuação é significativa na língua Suruí, não só porque nem sempre esta coincidência se verifica ... além de não haver como predizer onde cairá o acento nestas circunstâncias"
sources.locator: Ch. III-B 'Tom e acentuação; considerações de ritmo; efeitos dos enclíticos', pp. 24-30; '2) Acento' p. 26; position statement §a) p. 28 (scan pages p030, p032; verified against page images)
sources.note: Suruí is tonal (two underlying tones H/L, four surface pitch levels produced by the interaction of tone and stress). Word stress ('acento') is lexical and FREE in position ('parece ser livre'): it normally falls on a high-tone syllable but is not predictable from tone, since words may have no or several H syllables; the only constraint noted is that a final LOW-tone syllable, in a word that also has (non-proclitic) H syllables, can carry stress only if heavy (long vowel or closed). Three stress degrees (0, 1, 2 = sentence nucleus); stress shifts to the verb's last syllable before enclitics, a…

sources.citation: Guerra, Mariana de Lacerda (2004). Aspects of Suruí phonology and phonetics. DEA dissertation (dir. Didier Demolin, co-dir. Denny Moore), Laboratoire de Phonologie, Université Libre de Bruxelles, 105 pp. [Glottolog 305598/629856; not a sweep item — located during this sweep]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.quote: p. 54: "Surui language has two phonological level tones, high (H) and low (L). The TBU (tone bearing unit) in Surui is the vowel. There is one tone per vowel, no matter its length, consequently a vowel cannot bear two tones, creating contours ... As each syllable has one vowel only, the number of tones per word is the same as the number of vowels and the number of syllables of that word."
sources.locator: Ch. 4 'Tone', §4.1 p. 54 (scan p058); table of contents p. iv (scan p004)
sources.note: Silent on word stress: the whole thesis (vowels, consonants, tone phonology/phonetics, tone processes) never uses the words 'stress' or 'accent' (0 scanned hits over 105 pages; TOC has no stress section). It describes a two-level tone system with pitch measured on whistled and spoken monosyllables/disyllables and tone dissimilation rules. Does not engage van der Meer's stress analysis.

sources.citation: Surui, Tiago Iteor (2020). Descrevendo a língua dos Paiter Ej (Suruí de Rondônia): contribuições de um falante nativo. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade de Brasília, 106 pp. [Glottolog 589663; not a sweep item]
sources.quote: p. 19: "O segundo trabalho sobre a fonologia da língua Paiter consiste em uma dissertação de mestrado de autoria de Tine H. Van der Meer, defendida em Campinas em 1982, sob a orientação do Prof. Aryon Dall'Igna Rodrigues. ... O trabalho considera a sílaba e descreve suas características e padrões profundos e superficiais. Dá atenção especial ao tom e à acentuação e aos efeitos dos clíticos no ritmo dos enunciados." — Intro: "fizemos nossa própria análise fonológica segmental, mas não aprofundamos o sistema tonal da língua, de forma que os tons não são marcados nos dados da presente dissertação."
sources.locator: Introduction (p. 14-15 of PDF, 'Embora não tenhamos abordado a fonologia...'); literature review p. 19
sources.note: Second-hand only: no first-hand stress statement; the author explicitly leaves tone unmarked and does not treat phonology. Points to van der Meer 1982 as the source on tone and accentuation (now read, see above).

sources.citation: Yvinec, Cédric & Agamenon Gamasakaka Suruí (2017). Suruí of Rondônia. In K. Stenzel & B. Franchetto (eds.), On this and other worlds: Voices from Amazonia, 439-465. Berlin: Language Science Press. [Glottolog 552418; not a sweep item]
sources.quote: p. 441: "The tilde, acute accent, and circumflex denote nasalization, high tone on oral vowels, and high tone on nasalized vowels, respectively. Vowels without any diacritic mark are oral vowels with low (or undetermined) tone."
sources.note: Only the practical orthography's tone marking (acute = high tone, not stress); nothing on stress placement. Text collection, not a phonological description.
